text:
maya (Product): Quick sync on pool picker + autoscale controls. Did a 6-person usability run and found 3 recurring confusions: 'burst' vs 'temporary burst', slider labels, and confirmation wording. screenshots attached.
sam (PM): summary please — low on time.
maya (Product): tl;dr: change wording from 'Burst' to 'Burst (temporary)'; add tiny badge 'eligible' on pools; surface region tag inline; show a non-modal warning when min < 1 and burst > 4.
liam (Frontend): implementation notes: adding badge is trivial. Persistent shelf will need aria-live="polite" and rate-limited renders to avoid spamming SRs. Also we should keep list sort stable to avoid focus jumps.
frances (A11y): agree on aria-live="polite" for shelf. Also ensure slider handles announce values like 'Min GPUs: 2' on change and keyboard step is consistent.
anya (UX Research): users expected an explanation for why burst might fail. Suggest copy: 'Burst may be rejected if the target pool has no spare capacity.'
oliver (ML Infra): backend will return a reason code when migration denied. UI should show 'Reason: capacity' or 'Reason: policy' per code.
maya (Product): proposed copy for confirm modal: 'Move workload to pool "<name>" — expected start: ~2m. KV cache may be invalidated. If denied, fallback will remain on current pool.'
sam (PM): prefer inline helper rather than modal for simple moves. modal OK for cross-region moves.
liam (Frontend): I'll prototype shelf + helper copy by Thu EOD.
frances (A11y): include a short test checklist in PR: NVDA, VoiceOver, keyboard-only, focus order.
deploy-bot: FYI: Pool API schema change scheduled 03:00 UTC tomorrow. Mark feature branch protected until then.
maya (Product): cool. I'll update Figma + copy and loop in research for 5-user follow-up after prototype. :thumbsup:
